 SANGER, Calif. (FOX26) — California gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton brought his message on affordability to the Central Valley Thursday, October 29, hosting a public fuel giveaway at Loma Vista Travel Plaza in Sanger, where qualifying motorists were offered regular unleaded gasoline for just $3 per gallon.
 The event, held at 160 N. McCall Ave., attracted attention from drivers looking for relief from California's high gasoline prices.
 The promotion was limited to the first 150 vehicles, with a maximum purchase of 12 gallons per vehicle and one fill-up per person. 
 The offer applied exclusively to 87-octane regular unleaded gasoline, excluding premium, mid-grade and diesel.
 Steve Hilton rolled into Sanger with a $3 gas giveaway. (Photo: Courtesy FOX26 Photojournalist John Dwelle) 
 During the event, Hilton also outlined his proposals to abolish the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) and cap vehicle registration fees at $73.
 Hilton's proposals focused on reducing the financial burden on California motorists, who continue to face some of the highest gasoline prices in the country.
 Hilton pointed to state taxes, fees and energy regulations as contributing factors to the high cost of fuel.
 The Sanger appearance included a press conference, remarks from Hilton and a question-and-answer session with members of the media. 
 The event also provided opportunities for interviews with participating motorists and video footage of drivers filling up at the advertised $3-per-gallon price.
 Hilton used the event to highlight his campaign's focus on lowering transportation costs and making driving more affordable for California families, commuters and working residents.
 His proposed DMV overhaul and $73 vehicle registration cap add to his broader campaign message of reducing government costs and easing the financial pressures facing California households.
 The event placed gasoline affordability and vehicle-related expenses at the center of the gubernatorial campaign discussion in the Central Valley.
